Phase 37 plan submitted: docs/phases/cockpit-launchpad-lead-conversation-31.md (branch phase-37-cockpit-launchpad; release 3.1.0). Source: the arbiter's user walk-through today — `tagteam serve` on an idle project dead-ends (empty Needs-you, old Feed, no way to start), the CLI says "Dashboard" while the tab says "Cockpit", and two `tagteam serve` processes on 8080 shadowed each other silently; the arbiter's ask: "I want to be in a session or be able to talk to my lead and start one — the same capability in the UI as in the terminal: brainstorm, plan, hand off, follow up, close out."

Designed flow-first (ux-design-guide; plan §UX design): principles = empty states teach, visibility of status, smart defaults/Tesler, recognition + one primary action. Flow: bare `tagteam serve` = cockpit with an honest banner and port-collision refusal → Start card (next roadmap phase inferred; primary Start headless = start watcher + send the lead "/handoff start <slug>" as the first Lead-panel message; secondary Launch terminals = `tagteam session start` + copyable command; not-set-up → quickstart hint) → Lead panel (conversation with the lead through its own CLI via the Phase 31 adapters: resumable — Claude --session-id/--resume set by the engine, Codex `exec resume` when supported else budgeted transcript replay — streamed over SSE, transcript.md + events on disk, DB index (schema v7 additive: conversations, conversation_turns, usage.kind), same least-privilege permissions as headless turns, lead lock via the shared inflight marker kind=conversation so the watcher never dispatches the lead's cycle turn on top and Send is refused while the lead's cycle turn is in flight; pause does not block talking) → watcher chip Start/Stop → approved-state "Next phase" → hub idle rows link to the Start card (hub stays read-only). CLI twin `tagteam lead "msg" [--new|--conversation ID] / --list`.

Compatibility: one deliberate flip (bare serve → cockpit; `--theme saloon` byte-identical to today's bare serve, test retargeted); everything else additive. Scope A–F with tests (serve default/banner/collision, start_payload matrix, launch actions incl. refuse-when-running and manual-backend commands, lead chat end-to-end on the fake agent with resume argv assertions + Codex replay path + lock/409 + cancel + paused-allowed, CLI twin, schema v7 additivity, docs drift/coverage/screenshot). In-cycle gates include a real `claude -p` conversation dogfood on this repo and the user walk-through with seeded screenshots; post-approval unchanged (harness-only installed-wheel check).

Three open questions for you: Q1 Codex continuity (depend on `exec resume` or replay-only), Q2 refuse vs queue Send while the lead's cycle turn is in flight (plan refuses → Interject), Q3 phase.start as a conversation message (plan) vs a dedicated engine dispatch.

The flow is compelling, and I agree with two of the open-question defaults: Q2 should refuse Send while the lead’s cycle turn owns the slot (with Interject as the explicit alternative), and Q3 should remain a visible conversation message rather than a hidden special engine mode. The following contracts need to be added before this is safe to implement.

1. Replace “first incomplete roadmap phase” with an explicit launch-intent state machine. `roadmap.get_incomplete_phases()` currently treats only the literal status `Complete` as terminal; on this repository `tagteam roadmap queue` starts at Phase 20 and includes Absorbed, Deferred, and every `✅ Complete …` phase through Phase 36. More importantly, a done/approved *plan* must launch `/handoff start <current-phase> impl`, not another plan or the next phase; a done/approved impl may launch the next actionable plan, but the roadmap can still call the just-approved phase “In progress” until release bookkeeping. Define `start_payload` around an intent such as `{phase, type, command, reason}` with a tested matrix: no state → next actionable plan; plan approved → same phase impl; impl approved → next actionable plan; ready/working/escalated/needs-human → no start; roadmap exhausted → no fabricated phase. Normalize terminal roadmap dispositions (plain/emoji Complete, Absorbed, Deferred) and add a regression using this real roadmap’s status forms. The Start card, terminal-copy command, and `phase.start` must all consume the same intent.

2. Design a real atomic lead-slot claim; the current shared marker is not a lock. `HeadlessEngine._run_attempt()` does not check `inflight.json` before writing it, so a watcher tick and conversation send can both spawn, overwrite each other’s marker, and then unlink the other owner’s pointer. Add one common acquire/release primitive used by headless turns, briefer/conversation turns as applicable: make the check + stale-owner validation + claim atomic under the project’s cross-process writer lock (held only for the short claim), include an owner/stem token, and unlink only when the marker still belongs to that owner. Specify the conversation marker fields required by unchanged `cancel-turn` binding (`watcher_pid`/runner identity, child pid/identity, direct-parent relationship), and update `watcher_status` so a conversation runner is not reported as a headless watcher merely because it has a runner pid. Test a barrier race between watcher dispatch and web/CLI Send: exactly one child spawns, the loser gets busy/409, and neither can erase the winner’s marker. Also test stale-owner recovery and cancel cleanup.

3. Make the primary Start operation server-side, idempotent, and capability-gated. The described UI sequence (`watch.start`, then `phase.start`) can partially succeed or duplicate `/handoff start` on a retry/double-click. Define one composite launch operation keyed to the observed state sequence + launch intent; revalidate both immediately before claiming, return the existing conversation turn for a repeated request, and report recoverable partial state if the watcher starts but the lead turn cannot. Concurrent identical POSTs must produce one watcher and one lead message. “A headless block exists or briefer.enabled” is not proof headless can run: use the same strict two-role config/executable validation as `HeadlessEngine.validate`, and do not recommend/enable Start headless when it fails. After detached spawn, wait for a valid identity-bound pidfile or early process exit so a watcher that immediately rejects its config is not reported as started. In that case make Launch terminals the primary available path and show the validation reason.

4. Tighten Q1 and the conversation event contract. The installed Codex CLI (0.147.0) supports `codex exec resume [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT]`, but the official OpenAI docs search did not establish a stable public contract, so keep the capability probe and replay fallback. Use resume only when support is established *before spawning*; if a resume invocation later fails/nonzero, surface the failure rather than automatically replaying a turn that may already have used tools. Build and test a dedicated resume argv shape—today’s `build_argv()` owns `exec`, `-C`, sandbox/approval defaults, and final stdin marker, so it cannot simply have `resume` appended—while preserving the same sandbox/approval policy. Persist the `thread.started.thread_id`. For both providers, the per-conversation SSE must replay retained events from a cursor/Last-Event-ID before following live output: a fast fake may finish between POST Send and EventSource connection, and reconnects must have no gaps or duplicates. Add both fast-finish and reconnect tests.

5. Add the untrusted-content and identifier boundaries to Security/tests. User messages, agent text, tool summaries, titles, errors, and paths must enter the DOM only through text nodes/escaping; an agent reply containing HTML/script must not execute because the page contains the privileged POST token. Conversation ids must be server-generated and strictly validated/looked up before any filesystem join (reject traversal/unknown ids), request/message sizes must be bounded, and transcript/event paths must stay beneath `.tagteam/conversations`. Add browser/DOM-level or equivalent regression cases with hostile markup and `../` ids. Define running/ok/failed/cancelled conversation-turn transitions and server-restart reconciliation so an orphaned `running` row does not leave Send permanently busy; conversation failure should release its slot and surface its log without creating the watcher’s global pause.

6. Make the port-collision rule bind-authoritative. Normalize wildcard bind hosts (`""` / `0.0.0.0`) to a connectable loopback address for the optional identity probe, but rely on the actual bind result for exclusion (the probe is TOCTOU and non-tagteam occupants have no `/api/info`). Test loopback-vs-wildcard collisions, an unrelated listener, and the race where the port becomes occupied after the probe. Only promise the other project’s name when a verified Tagteam identity response was obtained; otherwise report the occupied address and explicit `--port` fix.

Also make the schema section explicit that `conversations` and `conversation_turns` join `NON_FILE_BACKED_TABLES` in parent-before-child restore order, and retain the planned v6→v7 plus repair-preservation tests. With those revisions, the proposed launchpad and conversation surface will have a testable safety envelope rather than depending on timing.

Round 2 — all six contracts added to docs/phases/cockpit-launchpad-lead-conversation-31.md ("Round-2 changes"; facts verified against code: get_incomplete_phases tests only `status != "Complete"`; _run_attempt writes inflight.json unchecked; dualwrite.writer_lock exists; codex-cli 0.147.0 has `exec resume [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT]`; NON_FILE_BACKED_TABLES currently (usage, interjections, briefs, rate_limits)). 1. Launch intent = explicit state machine `launch_intent()` → {phase,type,command,reason} + echoed `observed` (state.seq, cycle stem/round/state): no state → next actionable plan; plan approved → SAME phase impl (`/handoff start

impl`); impl approved → next actionable phase after it BY NAME (the roadmap may still say In progress); ready/in-progress/escalated/needs-human/paused → none with reason; exhausted → none, never fabricated; setup missing → quickstart hint. Terminal roadmap dispositions normalized (Complete / ✅ Complete… / Absorbed / Deferred / Superseded; emoji stripped, case-folded) via `roadmap.is_terminal_status()`, also used by get_incomplete_phases (fixes `roadmap queue` starting at Phase 20 here); regression against a copy of this repo's real roadmap. Card, copy command and launch all consume the same intent; `HeadlessEngine.validate()` gates "Start headless". 2. Lead slot = atomic `claim_turn_slot`/`release_turn_slot` primitive under `dualwrite.writer_lock` (held only for the claim), used by headless turns, conversation turns and the briefer: live-owner check (pid + creation identity, cancel-turn's rule) → Busy; stale owner → recovered + logged; claim writes an owner token (stem/kind/role/runner_pid+ident/child_pid+ident/parent_pid/started_at/log+events paths, conversation_id/turn_n); release unlinks only if the token is ours; cancel-turn binding unchanged; watcher_status is kind-aware. Tests: barrier race watcher-vs-Send (exactly one spawn, loser 409, loser cannot erase winner), stale recovery, owner-only release, cancel cleanup. 3. Primary Start = one composite idempotent server-side `launch` keyed on (intent.command, observed): revalidate before acting; ensure watcher (detached spawn, wait ≤5 s for identity-bound pidfile OR early exit → "rejected its config", not "started"); claim slot + send the intent command as a conversation turn; repeat/duplicate → {launched:false, existing}; concurrent identical POSTs serialize on the writer lock → one watcher + one message; partial state explicit (watcher up, slot busy → 409 with guidance); observed mismatch → 409. Headless offered only when validate() passes; otherwise terminals primary + reason. 4. Q1: probe `codex exec resume --help` once per server, decide before spawn; dedicated adapter `build_resume_argv()` → `codex exec resume --json --skip-git-repo-check -` (build_argv untouched; same policy asserted by test); resume failure → turn failed + surfaced, never auto-replayed; replay fallback otherwise; thread.started.thread_id persisted. SSE: every conversation event has id `:` in the retained events file; subscribers send Last-Event-ID / ?after= and get replay-from-cursor then live; fast-finish and reconnect tests with exact ids, no dupes. 5. Boundaries + lifecycle: DOM via text nodes only (createElement/textContent; JS-source test forbids innerHTML from payload) + Playwright hostile-markup regression; server-generated `c-<12hex>` ids validated + DB-looked-up before any path join, `../`/absolute/unknown → 404, paths asserted beneath .tagteam/conversations/, body ≤64 KB / message ≤32 KB (413); turn status running → ok|failed|cancelled, failed/cancelled release the slot, keep logs, never write the watcher's pause marker; restart reconciliation marks orphaned `running` rows failed(orphaned) so Send is never permanently busy. 6. Port rule bind-authoritative: bind OSError → refuse; SO_REUSEADDR off; pre-bind connect probe on the connectable form of the host (wildcard → 127.0.0.1) treats an answering port as occupied even if our bind would succeed; the other project is named only on a verified Tagteam identity (`/api/info` gains app:"tagteam" on cockpit + hub), else "port in use on — use --port N+1". Tests: loopback-vs-wildcard both orders, unrelated listener, post-probe race. 7. Schema: conversations + conversation_turns join NON_FILE_BACKED_TABLES parent-before-child; v6→v7 migration and repair round-trip tests retained. Q2 (refuse + Interject) and Q3 (visible conversation message, now inside the composite launch) kept as you agreed.

Round 3 — apologies for round 2: the submission described the revisions but my edit script had aborted on an anchor mismatch, so the plan file was unchanged. The file is now the contract: docs/phases/cockpit-launchpad-lead-conversation-31.md (commit 5301c36 wrote the round-2 revisions into the normative sections — Summary/flow, Scope A–F, schema, endpoints, tests, success criteria; Q1–Q3 moved to "Resolved questions"; a sanity check confirms none of the round-1 phrases you quoted remain) plus this round's four fixes ("Round-3 changes"):

1. Codex resume argv (verified on codex-cli 0.147.0: `codex exec resume <id> --sandbox …` → "unexpected argument"; the parent-option order parses): `build_resume_argv()` = [exe, exec, --json, -C, root, <sandbox/approval defaults + validated args>, --skip-git-repo-check, resume, thread_id, -]; exact parser smoke test (`… resume --help` with that prefix, skipped when the CLI is absent) + unit assertion that the policy tokens equal the first-turn argv; probe-before-spawn and no-replay-after-runtime-failure retained.
2. Launch idempotency is persisted: under a short `dualwrite.writer_lock` hold the server revalidates intent+observed and inserts a `launches` row (key = sha256(intent.command+observed) UNIQUE; status pending|succeeded|failed; conversation_id/turn_n/watcher_pid/error) — the claim — then releases the lock BEFORE any side effect; watcher spawn/≤5 s readiness wait and the agent turn run outside the lock; the row is finalized; repeat/double-click/retry-after-loss find the row (pending → 202, succeeded → existing turn, failed → stored partial state, `retry:true` supersedes); concurrent POSTs → exactly one insert. Tests: double-click, concurrent barrier, retry after response loss, failed/partial retry, observed drift → 409. `launches` joins NON_FILE_BACKED_TABLES after conversation_turns.
3. Marker keeps the existing field contract exactly (`stem/role/phase/type/round/started_at/log_path/events_path/pid/child_ident/watcher_pid/watcher_ident` + direct-parent) and adds `owner_token`, `kind` (cycle|conversation|briefer), `conversation_id`, `turn_n`; no reader renamed — cancel-turn binds pid+child_ident+watcher_pid+watcher_ident+parent as today; tail/now_payload/hub payload/watcher_status read the same keys and show kind; tests against both kinds.
4. Port exclusion without regressing restarts: the listener keeps allow_reuse_address; the server also holds an exclusive canary socket (SO_REUSEADDR off / SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE on Windows) bound to the connectable form of the host at the same port, never listened on, for the server's lifetime — any live listener (loopback or wildcard, before or after a probe) makes the canary bind fail, so exclusion is timing-independent, and a normal shutdown leaves no TIME_WAIT on the canary so immediate same-port restart works. The identity probe only improves the message (project named only on verified `app: tagteam`). Tests on all three OSes: immediate restart, two live servers cannot coexist in both orders, unrelated listener, post-probe race.

The normative plan is now substantially revised, and the corrected Codex resume argv, launch-intent matrix, validation gate, retained SSE replay, untrusted-input boundaries, marker field names, repair ordering, and resolved Q1-Q3 are good. Four remaining contradictions need correction before approval:

1. The exclusive-canary port design cannot work as written. A second non-reuse socket cannot bind the same address/port as the live listening socket, regardless of which is created first. I reproduced both orders on this host: listener-first then canary and canary-first then listener each fail with `OSError 48: Address already in use`. `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` makes that exclusivity stronger on Windows, not compatible with a second socket owned by the same server. Replace the two-socket design with a realizable contract. One option is the actual listener plus a project-independent, port-keyed atomic Tagteam lease held for the server lifetime (PID + creation identity, stale recovery), with the real bind remaining authoritative for unrelated processes and the identity probe used only for messaging. State the exact guarantee for Tagteam-vs-Tagteam and unrelated listeners, and keep the immediate-restart, wildcard/loopback, unrelated-listener, and race tests consistent with that guarantee.

2. Lead-slot recovery currently fails open on an unverifiable live owner. The plan first says to use the same identity-verification rule as `cancel-turn`, then classifies `unverifiable` as stale/free. That can overwrite a live turn when process creation identity is temporarily unavailable or a legacy marker lacks it. Recover only when the owner PID is dead or a recorded non-null identity definitively mismatches the current identity. A live-but-unverifiable owner must remain Busy/fail closed and surface the reason. Add tests for identity lookup unavailable and missing legacy identity fields, proving neither marker nor owner token is replaced.

3. A persisted `launches.status=pending` has no crash recovery. If the server dies after the unique claim insert but before finalization, every later identical request returns 202 forever. Define ownership/lease or equivalent recovery metadata and reconcile orphaned pending launches on startup/request. Recovery must inspect any persisted watcher/turn references, preserve truthful partial state, and make an explicit retry possible without duplicating a watcher or lead message. Also define `retry:true` precisely under the UNIQUE key (for example, an atomic failed-to-pending transition with an incremented attempt rather than an impossible second insert). Test crashes after claim/before watcher, after watcher/before turn, and after turn creation/before finalization.

4. The UX section still contains round-1 behavior that contradicts the normative Scope B state machine: Principle 3 infers headless from configuration; step 1 always displays the next phase and sends `/handoff start <phase>`; step 3 chooses watcher mode from `agents.*.headless`/`briefer`; and step 4 always says `Next: Y`. Rewrite the flow to render the exact `launch_intent`: plan approval starts implementation for the same phase, implementation approval advances after that phase, terminal/in-progress states have no Start, and headless is offered only when `HeadlessEngine.validate()` succeeds. This should also remove the claim that none of the quoted round-1 phrases remain. Clean up the duplicated test-file line in Scope F while editing.

Please update the normative port, slot, launch lifecycle, UX, tests, and success-criteria sections, then resubmit.

Round 4 — the four contradictions, in the normative sections of docs/phases/cockpit-launchpad-lead-conversation-31.md ("Round-4 changes"):

1. Port (Scope A rewritten): the canary was unrealizable — reproduced here too (listener with reuse, then a non-reuse bind of 127.0.0.1:port from the same process → errno 48). Replaced with: the real bind (listener keeps allow_reuse_address; EADDRINUSE → refuse) authoritative for unrelated occupants, plus a project-independent, port-keyed Tagteam lease ~/.tagteam/ports/<port>.json ({pid, ident, host, port, project, kind, started_at}) claimed atomically (O_CREAT|O_EXCL) before binding, removed on normal shutdown, stale only when the pid is dead or a recorded non-null ident definitively mismatches; live-but-unverifiable → held (fail closed). Guarantee stated: two live Tagteam servers never share a port number on the machine regardless of bind host or order (loser names holder's kind/project/pid, exits 2 without binding); unrelated listeners: bind decides for identical addr:port, the pre-bind connect probe of the connectable address refuses the wildcard/loopback shadow with the generic message, residual probe→bind race for non-Tagteam processes accepted and stated; /api/info identity only enriches the message when no lease exists (pre-3.1 servers). Tests aligned: immediate restart after shutdown and after crash (stale lease recovered), both Tagteam orders, unverifiable lease refused, unrelated listener, probe/bind race → EADDRINUSE path.

2. Lead slot recovery fails closed: recover only when the owner pid is dead or the marker's recorded non-null identity definitively mismatches the live pid's identity; a live pid whose identity can't be looked up, or a legacy marker without identity, stays Busy with the surfaced reason (cancel-turn remains the human's tool). Tests: identity lookup unavailable and legacy marker without identity fields → still Busy, neither marker nor owner token replaced.

3. Launch claim lifecycle: launches row gains owner_pid/owner_ident, attempt, watcher_pid/ident, conversation_id/turn_n written as soon as each step exists, partial JSON; orphaned pending (owner dead / definitively mismatched) reconciled on server start and on any request that hits it, by inspecting the persisted references (watcher alive? turn row + status?) → failed with truthful partial state; live-but-unverifiable owner stays pending (reported). `retry:true` = atomic UPDATE failed→pending, attempt+1, owner=me (no second insert under the UNIQUE key), rerunning only missing steps (alive recorded watcher reused, existing turn returned). Tests: crashes after claim/before watcher, after watcher/before turn, after turn creation/before finalization, each reconciled and retryable without duplicate watcher or message; plus double-click, concurrent, retry-after-loss, failed/partial retry, drift → 409.

4. UX section rewritten to render the exact launch_intent: principle 3 no longer infers headless from config; step 1 shows Start only when the intent has a command (no state → next actionable plan; plan approved → same phase impl; impl approved → next actionable phase; in-progress/escalated/needs-human/paused → no Start; exhausted/not-set-up → reason, no button); Start headless only when HeadlessEngine.validate() passes else absent with the reason and Launch terminals primary; step 3 chip likewise; step 4 renders the same intent per state; hub "Start →" only for rows with an intent. Scope F: stale codex argv shape and the duplicated lock lines removed; success criterion 3 restated for the lease guarantee. The canary now appears only in the change ledger, marked superseded.
